title: Edge multiplex proxy: scalable SSE/WSS session simulator for KV-aware token-throughput
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a high-fidelity, horizontally-scalable harness that simulates edge client behavior for streaming chat/completions over SSE and WebSocket. The harness must model multiplexed sessions, KV-cache hits/misses, soft connection churn, and token-level pacing to reproduce realistic tokens/sec and p95 tail latency at Redwood scale. This will replace several ad-hoc drivers and enable deterministic regression gates for CI and nightly performance runs.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can open 200k concurrent logical sessions across N nodes while maintaining <5% failure/connect error rate under normal simulated network jitter.
Can simulate prefix KV-cache hit ratio configuration per test (0%, 50%, 90%) and surface per-session cache metrics to validate cache-aware batching behavior.
Produces telemetry-compatible histograms for per-response p50/p90/p95/p99 (ms) and tokens/sec aggregated in Prometheus and OpenTelemetry exports.
Integrates with regression detector: a nightly run must compare p95 tokens/sec and response p95 against baseline and emit a regression ticket when >15% degradation or p95 latency regression of >20%.
Expose scenario definitions as declarative YAML with parameters: session_types, multiplex_factor, token_pacing_profile, kv_hit_rate, churn_pattern, model_profile.
Documentation and quickstart: README + example CI job + dashboard links.
test_scenarios: Baseline burst: 50k logical sessions, multiplex_factor=8, kv_hit_rate=90%, token_pacing=realistic-chat-slow, run=30m
Cold cache stress: 100k sessions, multiplex_factor=1, kv_hit_rate=0%, high concurrency, run=60m
Churned connections: 75k sessions with churn_pattern=zipf-connection-lifetime, simulate short lived clients and reconnections
Multiplex stress: 200k logical sessions across 32 nodes, multiplex_factor=16, measure head-of-line and per-stream p95
Mixed models: route 60% to quantized small model, 40% to large model to validate routing/fallback behavior
regression_rules: If nightly tokens_per_sec_total drops > 15% relative to baseline -> create regression ticket (P1) and attach raw traces.
If response_p95_ms increases > 20% relative to baseline and absolute p95 > 350ms -> block runtime release cutoff.
If connect_error_rate > 5% sustained for 10 minutes -> alert on-call and annotate run as unstable.
If kv_cache_hit_ratio delta causes >10% tokens/sec regression -> flag for cache tuning and routing investigation.
telemetry_and_outputs: Prometheus metrics endpoint per harness node (labels: scenario, model_profile, kv_hit_rate)
OTLP traces for 100% of coordinator events and sampled per-session token streams
Aggregated nightly report in BigQuery with raw per-session timelines for regression forensics
runbook: How to start: helm chart in infra/test-harness, env var SCENARIO_YAML points at S3. Steps: deploy 3 nodes for small run, 32 nodes for scale run. Collect artifacts: /var/log/harness/*.jsonl and prometheus scrape. Known flakiness: ephemeral port exhaustion on AWS CNI when >10k sockets per host; workaround: tune iptables conntrack and set multiplex_factor to reduce sockets.

notes: This harness aims to bridge gaps between synthetic token generators and real SDK traffic by modeling multiplexing and KV-cache effects. Keep tests parameterized so we can reuse for Dedicated capacity sizing and Private deployment throughput validation.
